text: We do not have a very short time assigned to us, but we lose a great deal of it.
author: Seneca
source: On the Shortness of Life 1, tr. Aubrey Stewart (1889)

text: While we are postponing, life speeds by.
author: Seneca

text: Hold every hour in your grasp.
author: Seneca

text: That which is an obstacle on the road helps us on this road.
author: Marcus Aurelius

text: No longer talk at all about the kind of man that a good man ought to be, but be such.
author: Marcus Aurelius

text: He has half the deed done, who has made a beginning.
author: Horace
source: Epistles 1.2, tr. C. Smart, rev. T. A. Buckley

text: The journey of a thousand li commenced with a single step.
author: Laozi
source: Tao Te Ching 64, tr. James Legge (1891)

text: Nothing, Lucilius, is ours, except time.
author: Seneca

text: Lay hold of to-day's task, and you will not need to depend so much upon to-morrow's.
author: Seneca

text: Everywhere means nowhere.
author: Seneca

text: For love of bustle is not industry,—it is only the restlessness of a hunted mind.
author: Seneca

text: He who would arrive at the appointed end must follow a single road and not wander through many ways.
author: Seneca

text: I force my mind to concentrate, and keep it from straying to things outside itself.
author: Seneca

text: When a man does not know what harbour he is making for, no wind is the right wind.
author: Seneca

text: Let us postpone nothing. Let us balance life's account every day.
author: Seneca

text: Nature has not given us such a generous and free-handed space of time that we can have the leisure to waste any of it.
author: Seneca

text: One who daily puts the finishing touches to his life is never in want of time.
author: Seneca

text: Life is long enough, if you know how to use it.
author: Seneca
source: On the Shortness of Life 2, tr. Aubrey Stewart (1889)

text: Remember how long thou hast been putting off these things.
author: Marcus Aurelius

text: Give thyself time to learn something new and good, and cease to be whirled around.
author: Marcus Aurelius

text: For the greatest part of what we say and do being unnecessary, if a man takes this away, he will have more leisure and less uneasiness.
author: Marcus Aurelius

text: In the morning when thou risest unwillingly, let this thought be present,—I am rising to the work of a human being.
author: Marcus Aurelius

text: Confine thyself to the present.
author: Marcus Aurelius

text: Attend to the matter which is before thee, whether it is an opinion or an act or a word.
author: Marcus Aurelius

text: Thou sufferest this justly: for thou choosest rather to become good to-morrow than to be good to-day.
author: Marcus Aurelius

text: Do not disturb thyself by thinking of the whole of thy life.
author: Marcus Aurelius

text: He who follows reason in all things is both tranquil and active at the same time, and also cheerful and collected.
author: Marcus Aurelius

text: When you have remitted your attention for a short time, do not imagine this, that you will recover it when you choose.
author: Epictetus

text: If you would be a good reader, read; if a writer, write.
author: Epictetus

text: Men are disturbed not by the things which happen, but by the opinions about the things.
author: Epictetus

text: All great things are slow of growth; nay, this is true even of a grape or of a fig.
author: Epictetus

text: He who overcomes others is strong; he who overcomes himself is mighty.
author: Laozi
source: Tao Te Ching 33, tr. James Legge (1891)

text: Though but one basketful is thrown at a time, the advancing with it is my own going forward.
author: Confucius

text: Desire to have things done quickly prevents their being done thoroughly.
author: Confucius

text: The mechanic, who wishes to do his work well, must first sharpen his tools.
author: Confucius

text: Even by the falling of water-drops a water-pot is filled; the wise man becomes full of good, even if he gather it little by little.
author: The Dhammapada

text: It is good to tame the mind, which is difficult to hold in and flighty, rushing wherever it listeth; a tamed mind brings happiness.
author: The Dhammapada

text: As a solid rock is not shaken by the wind, wise people falter not amidst blame and praise.
author: The Dhammapada

text: While we stop to think, we often miss our opportunity.
author: Publilius Syrus

text: Yesterday should be the teacher of to-day.
author: Publilius Syrus

text: They live ill who expect to live always.
author: Publilius Syrus

text: Many things which cannot be overcome when they are together, yield themselves up when taken little by little.
author: Plutarch
source: Life of Sertorius, tr. Dryden, rev. A. H. Clough (1864)

text: While we are conversing, envious age has been flying; seize the present day, not giving the least credit to the succeeding one.
author: Horace
source: Odes 1.11, tr. C. Smart, rev. T. A. Buckley

text: They change their climate, not their disposition, who run beyond the sea.
author: Horace
source: Epistles 1.11, tr. C. Smart, rev. T. A. Buckley

text: Winged time glides on insensibly and deceives us; and there is nothing more fleeting than years.
author: Ovid

text: But hasten, and do not postpone to a future moment; that which is not agreeable to-day, will to-morrow be still less so.
author: Ovid
source: Remedy of Love, tr. Henry T. Riley (1885)

text: Men come to be builders, for instance, by building; harp-players, by playing on the harp.
author: Aristotle
source: Nicomachean Ethics 2.1, tr. D. P. Chase (1847)

text: It is not one swallow or one fine day that makes a spring, so it is not one day or a short time that makes a man blessed and happy.
author: Aristotle
source: Nicomachean Ethics 1.7, tr. D. P. Chase (1847)

text: Our life is frittered away by detail. … Simplify, simplify.
author: Henry David Thoreau

text: It is not enough to be industrious; so are the ants. What are you industrious about?
author: Henry David Thoreau
source: Letter to H. G. O. Blake, Nov. 16, 1857, Familiar Letters

text: Nothing so fatiguing as the eternal hanging on of an uncompleted task.
author: William James
source: Letter to Carl Stumpf, Jan. 1, 1886, The Letters of William James (1920)

text: Lost time is never found again.
author: Benjamin Franklin

text: Dost thou love life? Then do not squander time, for that's the stuff life is made of.
author: Benjamin Franklin

text: You may delay, but time will not.
author: Benjamin Franklin

text: Do the thing, and you shall have the power.
author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

text: Nothing can bring you peace but yourself.
author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

text: I'm not afraid of storms, for I'm learning how to sail my ship.
author: Louisa May Alcott

text: What we call time enough, always proves little enough.
author: Benjamin Franklin

text: Drive thy business, let not that drive thee.
author: Benjamin Franklin

text: One today is worth two tomorrows.
author: Benjamin Franklin

text: Little strokes fell great oaks.
author: Benjamin Franklin

text: Since thou art not sure of a minute, throw not away an hour.
author: Benjamin Franklin

text: Leisure is time for doing something useful.
author: Benjamin Franklin

text: Lose no time; be always employed in something useful; cut off all unnecessary actions.
author: Benjamin Franklin

text: Be not disturbed at trifles, or at accidents common or unavoidable.
author: Benjamin Franklin

text: As if you could kill time without injuring eternity.
author: Henry David Thoreau

text: Time is but the stream I go a-fishing in.
author: Henry David Thoreau

text: Let us spend one day as deliberately as Nature.
author: Henry David Thoreau

text: Why should we live with such hurry and waste of life?
author: Henry David Thoreau

text: A man is rich in proportion to the number of things which he can afford to let alone.
author: Henry David Thoreau

text: Morning is when I am awake and there is a dawn in me.
author: Henry David Thoreau

text: I love a broad margin to my life.
author: Henry David Thoreau

text: Things do not change; we change.
author: Henry David Thoreau

text: The years teach much which the days never know.
author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

text: To fill the hour, that is happiness; to fill the hour and leave no crevice for a repentance or an approval.
author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

text: The one prudence in life is concentration; the one evil is dissipation.
author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

text: Write it on your heart that every day is the best day in the year.
author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

text: He only is rich who owns the day.
author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

text: Adopt the pace of Nature. Her secret is patience.
author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

text: My experience is what I agree to attend to.
author: William James

text: The faculty of voluntarily bringing back a wandering attention, over and over again, is the very root of judgment, character, and will.
author: William James

text: Never suffer an exception to occur till the new habit is securely rooted in your life.
author: William James

text: Seize the very first possible opportunity to act on every resolution you make.
author: William James

text: Keep the faculty of effort alive in you by a little gratuitous exercise every day.
author: William James

text: If he keep faithfully busy each hour of the working-day, he may safely leave the final result to itself.
author: William James

text: Leave nothing for tomorrow which can be done today.
author: Abraham Lincoln
source: Notes for a Law Lecture (1850), Complete Works, vol. 2 (1894)

text: Whatever piece of business you have in hand, before stopping, do all the labor pertaining to it which can then be done.
author: Abraham Lincoln
source: Notes for a Law Lecture (1850), Complete Works, vol. 2 (1894)

text: Habit is habit, and not to be flung out of the window by any man, but coaxed downstairs a step at a time.
author: Mark Twain

text: Happiness, knowledge, not in another place but this place, not for another hour but this hour.
author: Walt Whitman
source: "A Song for Occupations," Leaves of Grass (1891–92)

text: Not knowing when the dawn will come / I open every door.
author: Emily Dickinson

text: Let us, then, be up and doing, / With a heart for any fate; / Still achieving, still pursuing, / Learn to labor and to wait.
author: Henry Wadsworth Longfellow

text: Look not mournfully into the Past. It comes not back again. Wisely improve the Present. It is thine.
author: Henry Wadsworth Longfellow

text: I find the great thing in this world is not so much where we stand, as in what direction we are moving.
author: Oliver Wendell Holmes Sr.
source: The Autocrat of the Breakfast-Table, ch. 4 (1858)

text: Nothing ever comes to me, that is worth having, except as the result of hard work.
author: Booker T. Washington

text: It is at the bottom of life we must begin, and not at the top.
author: Booker T. Washington

text: I go to Nature to be soothed and healed, and to have my senses put in tune once more.
author: John Burroughs
source: "The Gospel of Nature," Time and Change (1912)

text: There is time enough for everything, in the course of the day, if you do but one thing at once.
author: Lord Chesterfield

text: I recommend to you to take care of the minutes; for hours will take care of themselves.
author: Lord Chesterfield

text: Know the true value of time; snatch, seize, and enjoy every moment of it.
author: Lord Chesterfield

text: Whatever is worth doing at all, is worth doing well; and nothing can be done well without attention.
author: Lord Chesterfield

text: The trifling and frivolous mind is always busied, but to little purpose.
author: Lord Chesterfield

text: Great works are performed not by strength, but perseverance.
author: Samuel Johnson

text: He that shall walk with vigour three hours a day, will pass in seven years a space equal to the circumference of the globe.
author: Samuel Johnson

text: Few things are impossible to diligence and skill.
author: Samuel Johnson

text: Many of our hours are lost in a rotation of petty cares, in a constant recurrence of the same employments.
author: Samuel Johnson

text: For every single act of progression a short time is sufficient.
author: Samuel Johnson

text: Idleness never can secure tranquillity.
author: Samuel Johnson

text: The soul that has no established aim loses itself.
author: Michel de Montaigne
source: Essays I.8, "Of Idleness," tr. Charles Cotton, ed. W. C. Hazlitt (1877)

text: When I dance, I dance; when I sleep, I sleep.
author: Michel de Montaigne
source: Essays III.13, "Of Experience," tr. Charles Cotton, ed. W. C. Hazlitt (1877)

text: Have you known how to take repose, you have done more than he who has taken empires and cities.
author: Michel de Montaigne
source: Essays III.13, "Of Experience," tr. Charles Cotton, ed. W. C. Hazlitt (1877)

text: I have discovered that all the unhappiness of men arises from one single fact, that they cannot stay quietly in their own chamber.
author: Blaise Pascal
source: Pensées, no. 139, tr. W. F. Trotter (1910)

text: So imprudent are we that we wander in the times which are not ours, and do not think of the only one which belongs to us.
author: Blaise Pascal
source: Pensées, no. 172, tr. W. F. Trotter (1910)

text: It is not enough to know, we must also apply; it is not enough to will, we must also do.
author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe
source: Maxims and Reflections, no. 324, tr. Bailey Saunders (1893)

text: What is your duty? The claims of the day.
author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe
source: Maxims and Reflections, no. 3, tr. Bailey Saunders (1893)

text: Nothing is more highly to be prized than the value of each day.
author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe
source: Maxims and Reflections, no. 332, tr. Bailey Saunders (1893)

text: Unqualified activity, of whatever kind, leads at last to bankruptcy.
author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe
source: Maxims and Reflections, no. 9, tr. Bailey Saunders (1893)

text: Procrastination is the thief of time. Collar him!
author: Charles Dickens

text: There is no substitute for thorough-going, ardent, and sincere earnestness.
author: Charles Dickens

text: Patience and time are my warriors, my champions.
author: Leo Tolstoy
source: War and Peace, bk. 13, ch. 17, tr. Louise and Aylmer Maude (1922)

text: There is no greatness where simplicity, goodness, and truth are absent.
author: Leo Tolstoy
source: War and Peace, bk. 14, ch. 18, tr. Louise and Aylmer Maude (1922)

text: What is needed is constant work, day and night, constant reading, study, will.... Every hour is precious for it.
author: Anton Chekhov
source: Letter to his brother Nikolay, 1886, tr. Constance Garnett (1920)

text: You must love your work, and not be always looking over the edge of it, wanting your play to begin.
author: George Eliot

text: Lost wealth may be replaced by industry, lost knowledge by study, lost health by temperance or medicine, but lost time is gone for ever.
author: Samuel Smiles

text: An economical use of time is the true mode of securing leisure.
author: Samuel Smiles

text: Talkers may sow, but the silent reap.
author: Samuel Smiles

text: The water you touch in a river is the last of that which has passed, and the first of that which is coming. Thus it is with time present.
author: Leonardo da Vinci
source: Notebooks, no. 1174, tr. Jean Paul Richter (1883)

text: Life if well spent, is long.
author: Leonardo da Vinci
source: Notebooks, no. 1174, tr. Jean Paul Richter (1883)

text: Just as iron rusts unless it is used, and water putrifies or, in cold, turns to ice, so our intellect spoils unless it is kept in use.
author: Leonardo da Vinci
source: Notebooks, no. 1177, tr. Jean Paul Richter (1883)

text: To choose time, is to save time; and an unseasonable motion, is but beating the air.
author: Francis Bacon

text: Measure not dispatch, by the times of sitting, but by the advancement of the business.
author: Francis Bacon

text: We have all a better guide in ourselves, if we would attend to it, than any other person can be.
author: Jane Austen

text: Know your own happiness. You want nothing but patience—or give it a more fascinating name, call it hope.
author: Jane Austen

text: All books are divisible into two classes, the books of the hour, and the books of all time.
author: John Ruskin

text: The newspaper may be entirely proper at breakfast time, but assuredly it is not reading for all day.
author: John Ruskin

text: When we build, let us think that we build for ever.
author: John Ruskin
source: The Seven Lamps of Architecture, "The Lamp of Memory" (1849)

text: Do the Duty which lies nearest thee, which thou knowest to be a Duty! Thy second Duty will already have become clearer.
author: Thomas Carlyle

text: Silence is the element in which great things fashion themselves together.
author: Thomas Carlyle

text: Blessed is he who has found his work; let him ask no other blessedness.
author: Thomas Carlyle

text: Philosophers have explained space. They have not explained time. It is the inexplicable raw material of everything.
author: Arnold Bennett
source: How to Live on 24 Hours a Day, ch. 1 (1908)

text: You cannot waste to-morrow; it is kept for you.
author: Arnold Bennett
source: How to Live on 24 Hours a Day, ch. 1 (1908)

text: Dear sir, you simply begin. There is no magic method of beginning.
author: Arnold Bennett
source: How to Live on 24 Hours a Day, ch. 3 (1908)

text: You can turn over a new leaf every hour if you choose.
author: Arnold Bennett
source: How to Live on 24 Hours a Day, ch. 3 (1908)

text: Beware of undertaking too much at the start. Be content with quite a little.
author: Arnold Bennett
source: How to Live on 24 Hours a Day, ch. 3 (1908)

text: I do not care what you concentrate on, so long as you concentrate.
author: Arnold Bennett
source: How to Live on 24 Hours a Day, ch. 7 (1908)

text: The load of to-morrow, added to that of yesterday, carried to-day makes the strongest falter.
author: William Osler
source: A Way of Life, part III (1913)

text: The future is to-day—there is no to-morrow!
author: William Osler
source: A Way of Life, part III (1913)

text: Realise how much time there is, how long the day is.
author: William Osler
source: A Way of Life, part IV (1913)

text: The quiet life in day-tight compartments will help you to bear your own and others' burdens with a light heart.
author: William Osler
source: A Way of Life, part V (1913)

text: When you work you are a flute through whose heart the whispering of the hours turns to music.
author: Kahlil Gibran

text: Work is love made visible.
author: Kahlil Gibran

text: Yesterday is but today's memory and tomorrow is today's dream.
author: Kahlil Gibran

text: In the dew of little things the heart finds its morning and is refreshed.
author: Kahlil Gibran

text: Tiny grass, your steps are small, but you possess the earth under your tread.
author: Rabindranath Tagore

text: The noise of the moment scoffs at the music of the Eternal.
author: Rabindranath Tagore

text: The song that I came to sing remains unsung to this day. I have spent my days in stringing and in unstringing my instrument.
author: Rabindranath Tagore

text: The butterfly counts not months but moments, and has time enough.
author: Rabindranath Tagore

text: As a river in the sea, work finds its fulfilment in the depth of leisure.
author: Rabindranath Tagore

text: Until thought is linked with purpose there is no intelligent accomplishment.
author: James Allen
source: As a Man Thinketh, "Thought and Purpose" (1903)

text: Calmness of mind is one of the beautiful jewels of wisdom.
author: James Allen

text: Success is jealous of scattered energies.
author: Orison Swett Marden

text: To travel hopefully is a better thing than to arrive, and the true success is to labour.
author: Robert Louis Stevenson

text: He sows hurry and reaps indigestion.
author: Robert Louis Stevenson

text: Concentrate all your thought upon the work in hand. The sun's rays do not burn until brought to a focus.
author: Alexander Graham Bell
source: Interview in Marden, How They Succeeded, ch. 2 (1901)

text: It is hard to fail, but it is worse never to have tried to succeed.
author: Theodore Roosevelt

text: No pessimist ever discovered the secrets of the stars, or sailed to an uncharted land, or opened a new heaven to the human spirit.
author: Helen Keller

text: The best way out is always through.
author: Robert Frost
source: "A Servant to Servants", North of Boston (1914)

text: An inch of time is like an inch of gold.
author: Chinese proverb
source: Scarborough, A Collection of Chinese Proverbs, no. 2448 (1875)

text: In hurry is error.
author: Chinese proverb
source: Scarborough, A Collection of Chinese Proverbs, no. 89 (1875)

text: When the melon is ripe it will drop of itself.
author: Chinese proverb
source: Scarborough, A Collection of Chinese Proverbs, no. 755 (1875)

text: In calmness heaven and earth seem greater; in leisure days and months seem longer.
author: Chinese proverb
source: Scarborough, A Collection of Chinese Proverbs, no. 2459 (1875)

text: The feet of a heron standing in the water, rising to fly, roil not the stream.
author: Japanese proverb

text: At the bottom of patience there is heaven.
author: Kanuri proverb
source: Burton, Wit and Wisdom from West Africa, ch. 2, no. 7 (1865)

text: He who waits for chance may wait a year.
author: Yoruba proverb
source: Burton, Wit and Wisdom from West Africa, ch. 5, no. 38 (1865)

text: He that hunts two hares will catch neither.
author: French proverb
source: Bohn, A Polyglot of Foreign Proverbs (1857)

text: Little by little the bird builds its nest.
author: French proverb
source: Bohn, A Polyglot of Foreign Proverbs (1857)

text: With patience and time the mulberry leaf becomes a silk gown.
author: German proverb
source: Bohn, A Polyglot of Foreign Proverbs (1857)

text: Who goes softly goes safely, and he that goes safely goes far.
author: Italian proverb
source: Bohn, A Polyglot of Foreign Proverbs (1857)

text: The feed will still be there. This moment won't.
You came here to do something. Go do it.
Close the tab. Open the work.
Boredom is the doorway. Walk through it into the work.
